To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a system that allows a mobile manipulation robot to pick and place novel unknown objects in unstructured human environments.

(1) mobile manipulation in unstructured human environments can be accomplished using a combination of visual, tactile, proprioceptive, and reactive sensing and control; (2) reactive control and monitoring can be effectively used to compensate for the uncertainty arising from noisy sensor data; (3) a combination of 3-D and 2-D visual processing is required to effectively perceive the environment, and (4) a modular, easily configurable software architecture is necessary for rapid deployment of a mobile manipulation system in new environments
we have developed a robust system for mobile manipulation in unstructured environments that can be easily re-configured for new systems.

enabling robots to manipulate objects in unstructured human environments.
the development of a mobile manipulation system that is robust to uncertainty in perception, motion, and control.
enabling a robot to operate in unstructured human environments by providing it with a set of tools to perceive, plan, and execute tasks in such environments.
